text:
jena: Heads up — saw a spike (~2.3k req/s) where a bunch of EU customers got routed to us-east and then immediately rerouted back, causing p95 to spike and quota churn. Logs show rapid variant swaps within ~200ms.

matt: can you paste a couple sample req ids?

jena: sample ids: r-4b7a, r-4b7b. excerpt from router trace: 
```
router.trace { req_id: r-4b7a, initial_region: eu-west, chosen_region: us-east, chosen_variant: v1-small, fallback_variant: v2-q, elapsed_ms: 210 }
```

srebot: alert: routing-anomaly detected EU->us-east (count=2300) :rotating_light:

kai: looking at router logs — the new "global_preference" ranking was evaluated before the regional affinity check. that means cheaper variants in remote regions can win even when a local-compatible variant exists.

ben: that was my change from yesterday (PR #5487). I added a preference for cost-ranked candidates; I didn't realize it could short-circuit region-affinity. my bad.

matt: the symptom is a short-lived oscillation: request goes eu->us-east (cheaper), hits capacity or quant mismatch, falls back to eu variant, but the retry policy re-evaluates and picks us-east again because the global flag has very low TTL. result: a tiny loop that amplifies across many requests (variant echo).

emily: urgent mitigations we can do now: 1) flip off global_preference, 2) increase fallback backoff and introduce a sticky TTL per request key (fallback_lock=30s), 3) emit a dedicated metric for fallback loop count.

jena: agreed. immediate plan: 
- disable global_preference flag in router config (hot)
- set fallback_backoff_ms = 1000 from 50 (hot)
- add metric: routing.fallback.loop.count (hot)

kai: wrote a short patch to re-order the checks. snippet: 
```
# old logic
if (rank.global_preference) {
  route = pick_cheapest(route_candidates)
}
# new logic
if (region_affinity.same_region) {
  if (rank.global_preference) route = pick_cheapest(route_candidates)
} else {
  route = enforce_region_affinity(route_candidates) // prefer same-region unless explicitly allowed
}
```

ben: rolling the hotfix to canary now. deploying router rtr-5487-hotfix -> canary (10%). :hammer_and_wrench:

srebot: deploybot: canary rollout started rtr-5487-hotfix (canary=10%) :white_check_mark:

matt: console/UX followup: we need a clear toggle in the rollout UI called "regional tie-breaker" and show the full fallback chain in per-request traces so SREs can eyeball variant-chains quickly. open to suggestions for where in the UI.

anya: also add an alert: routing.fallback.rate > 1% per minute per customer — that would have flagged this earlier.

emily: TODOs captured: add telemetry labels route_origin, fallback_reason, variant_chain_length; create dashboard tiles: "variant chain length (p99)" and "cross-geo reroutes / min" and attach alerting.

matt: +1. Also add a cheap synthetic test that sends eu-only traffic and asserts no us-east hops. run as part of post-deploy smoke.

jena: thanks. immediate follow-up: monitor canary for 15m; if fallback loop metric stays low we proceed to full rollout. will draft a short postmortem if hotfix doesn't fix by EOD. :coffee:

ben: hotfix id rtr-5487-hotfix. canary metrics will post to #eng-platform-metrics.

srebot: canary metrics: fallback.loop.count -> 0.08% at 10m mark :bar_chart:

matt: canary stable. starting progressive rollout to 50% now. :rocket:

jena: closing for now. moving action items to eng-platform board: link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2129

ben: thanks everyone, sorry for the churn.

emily: we'll follow up with a small UX ticket for the tie-breaker toggle and a docs blurb on how fallback policies interact with region affinity.

jena: ending thread — will ping if anything else pops up.
